extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry / specialists studying Mochizuki's IUT
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and understanding definitions, structural properties, and propositions about multiradial/uniradial functors, radial environments, and various cyclotomic rigidity results appearing in the IUT exposition (sections on multiradiality, LCFT variants, and constant-multiple rigidity).

rubrics_metrics.name: multiradial (definition)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being multiradial means the radial algorithm/functor is full. Consequences discussed: liftability of isomorphisms (makes possible a kind of parallel transport from another radial data via associated coric data), switching functor preserves isomorphism classes (so one can 'switch' radial data up to isomorphism), and in the final multiradial algorithm theta-values (pilot objects) on two sides become indistinguishable up to mild indeterminacies, yielding bounds for height functions. Examples: a tautologically multiradial replacement in holomorphic structures or full-poly isomorphism cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: uniradial (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: (cid:8) is uniradial, if (cid:8) is not full.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the radial algorithm is uniradial then an isomorphism in C need not come from an isomorphism in R: objects of R lose part of rigidity and may be subject to additional indeterminacy. Example: underlying real 2-space R^2 with holomorphic structures — the forgetful functor from 1-dim C-vector spaces to underlying R-vector spaces is uniradial (cannot see one holomorphic structure from another). For cyclotomic rigidity via LCFT, the radial environment can be uniradial because value-group data interacts with coric data and causes harmful effects; admitting certain indeterminacies can make it tautologically multiradial.

rubrics_metrics.name: radial environment (terminology)
rubrics_metrics.description: A radial environment is the triple (R; C; (cid:8)) where R is a radial category (radial data), C is a coric category (coric data), and (cid:8) is a radial algorithm/functor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The same triple is called a multiradial (resp. uniradial) environment if (cid:8) is multiradial (resp. uniradial). The text uses this setup to compare analytic/holomorphic/arithmetic structures and to state group-theoretic reconstructions and rigidity results.

rubrics_metrics.name: corically defined (coric) functor
rubrics_metrics.description: (cid:9)R is corically defined (or coric) if (cid:9)R has a factorisation (cid:4)R ◦ (cid:8), where (cid:4)R : C → yR is a functor, and the diagram R --(cid:9)R→ yR and R --(cid:8)→ C --(cid:4)R→ yR is 1-commutative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a precise condition when a lifting/definition of a functor between radial data factors through the coric data; used to characterize when diagrams commute up to 1-isomorphism and when constructions are 'corically' induced.

rubrics_metrics.name: graph of a functor (Graph((cid:4)))
rubrics_metrics.description: Graph((cid:4)) is the category whose objects are pairs (R, (cid:4)(R)) for R ∈ Ob(R), and whose morphisms are pairs (f : R → R', (cid:4)(f) : (cid:4)(R) → (cid:4)(R')).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to form commutative diagrams of natural functors R → Graph((cid:4)) ← C and to define the natural functor (cid:9)(cid:4) : R → Graph((cid:4)). The graph construction is used repeatedly to describe how radial data maps into coric data and to define 'multiradially defined' functors.

rubrics_metrics.name: multiradially deﬁned / multiradially defined functor
rubrics_metrics.description: Given yR a groupoid with all objects isomorphic, y(cid:8) : yR → C essentially surjective and (cid:9)R : R → yR a functor, (cid:9)R is multiradially defined (resp. uniradially defined) if (cid:8) is multiradial (resp. uniradial) and the diagram R --(cid:9)R→ yR --y(cid:8)→ C and R --(cid:8)→ C is 1-commutative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This formalizes when a functor from R to an auxiliary groupoid yR realizes the multiradiality property relative to the original coric functor (cid:8), allowing constructions of auxiliary categories and factors to be treated as multiradial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiradial Mono-theta Cyclotomic Rigidity (Proposition 11.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given tempered fundamental groups (cid:5)v of local model objects X for v ∈ Vbad and certain group-theoretically reconstructed quotients ((cid:5)v (cid:16))Gv, one constructs categories C', R(cid:2), E, functors (cid:8)(cid:2), (cid:4)(cid:2), (cid:9)(cid:4)(cid:2) etc., so that the radial environment (R(cid:2); C'; (cid:8)(cid:2)) is multiradial and (cid:9)(cid:4)(cid:2) is multiradially defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a named rigidity result: it lays out precise categorical objects (C', R(cid:2), E, and associated functors) and claims functorial group-theoretic reconstructions that make the environment multiradial. The proposition includes detailed structural descriptions of objects and morphisms in these categories (topological groups, ind-topological modules, cyclotomes, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiradial LCFT Cyclotomic Rigidity with Indeterminacies (Proposition 11.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: A variant of Proposition 11.4 in which the categories and objects incorporate LCFT-type objects (O(cid:3)((cid:5)), Ocgp(G), bZ(cid:2)-orbits) yielding a radial environment (RLCFT; C'; (cid:8)LCFT) that is multiradial, and a functor (cid:9)(cid:4)LCFT is multiradially defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This proposition explains how admitting certain indeterminacies (e.g. bZ(cid:2)-orbits / full poly-isomorphisms) and replacing O(cid:3)((cid:0)) by O(cid:2)((cid:0)) makes the LCFT-type cyclotomic rigidity tautologically multiradial. It specifies the objects/morphisms concretely (ind-topological monoids, group actions) and the functors between categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: pointed inversion automorphism / decomposition group (Definition 11.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given hyperbolic orbicurves Xv and certain rational points and coverings, there is a unique automorphism (cid:19)X of Xv of order 2 and corresponding outer automorphisms of reconstructed tempered fundamental groups/coverings; the decomposition group D((cid:22)(cid:0)) is defined for the chosen rational point and is determined up to (cid:1)temp-conjugacy. A pointed inversion automorphism is the triple (2 Aut((cid:127)Y); (cid:19)(cid:127)Y; ((cid:22)(cid:0))(cid:127)Y ) or variants described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defines the notion of pointed inversion automorphism used later in rigidity/constant-multiple constructions. The Definition includes conditions about stabilisation of special fiber graphs, fixed points under the involution, and uniqueness up to conjugacy; also explains when an étale theta function of standard type restricts to certain prescribed values on the decomposition group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiradial Constant Multiple Rigidity (Proposition 11.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists a functorial group-theoretic algorithm reconstructing, from a topological group (cid:5) isomorphic to (cid:5)temp_X_v (v ∈ Vbad), a commutative diagram relating O(cid:2)((cid:5)), O(cid:2)(M(cid:2)(cid:3)((cid:5))) and H^1-type limits, defining submodules O(cid:2)(M(...)) and O(cid:2)_1(...), and producing pointed inversion automorphisms and canonical splittings. This assignment yields a functor (cid:4)env : R(cid:2) → E_env and the natural functor is multiradially defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposition gives constructive algorithms: (1) reconstruct subsets/submodules so certain vertical arrows are isomorphisms; (2) construct pointed inversion automorphisms from topological groups; (3) restrict to decomposition subgroups and obtain splittings of O(...) subsets; (4) assign to an object of the radial category the projective systems, subsets, splittings, diagrams and poly-isomorphisms needed. The result is used to produce functorial splittings and multiradial definitions in subsequent structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hodge-Arakelov-theoretic evaluation and Gaussian monoids (section intro & Definition 11.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform Hodge–Arakelov-theoretic evaluation and construct Gaussian monoids at bad places v ∈ Vbad. For a hyperbolic orbicurve X_v over K_v, define the dual graph of the special fiber and certain distinguished connected subgraphs ( (cid:0)I_X, (cid:0)(cid:15)_X ) stabilised by the involution, and use these to form finite connected subgraphs in coverings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section explains how theta classes and theta evaluations are transported from group-theoretic situations to mono-theta environments and Frobenioid-theoretic situations via the functors (cid:5) ↦ M and F ↦ M, leading to F-theoretic and M-theoretic Gaussian monoids. The evaluation maps are compared to comparison maps in p-adic Hodge theory; the definition of special-subgraph pieces is used in defining local objects for Gaussian monoids and evaluations.
